label: UK INDUSTRIAL
headline: Ecommerce business SSS almost triples footprint at Indurent Park Burton
summary: Super Smart Service (SSS) has signed a 15-year lease on the 175,356 sq ft Unit B173 at Indurent Park Burton, West Midlands, nearly tripling its presence on the park. The unit is EPC A+ and targeting BREEAM Excellent. Indurent says SSS has taken around 1.75m sq ft of UK space this year.
key_figures: 175,356 sq ft; 15-year lease; c.1.75m sq ft taken by SSS in 2026; rent not disclosed
relevance: Big-box take-up by e-commerce on new-build, A-rated stock at a Midlands logistics hub.
why_matters: One occupier taking about 1.75m sq ft in a year is a material share of UK big-box demand. It supports the case for new-build Grade A space on M6/M1 corridors, which the North West competes for, even as investment yields soften.

label: NORTH WEST INDUSTRIAL
headline: Glencar progresses construction of bulk storage development for Peel Ports Group
summary: Contractor Glencar is building two bulk storage warehouses, Alexandra Warehouses 6 and 7, at Alexandra Dock, Liverpool, for Peel Ports Group. They will provide 131,730 sq ft of internal storage within a wider 249,529 sq ft development including infrastructure and access works, with about 60,000 tonnes of dry-bulk capacity.
key_figures: 131,730 sq ft storage; 249,529 sq ft wider development; c.60,000 tonnes capacity
relevance: Port-centric supply adds to constrained Merseyside warehouse stock; owner-occupier development rather than investment stock.
why_matters: It is new North West supply above 100,000 sq ft at a time when the region is short of Grade A space. Port-centric storage can relieve inland demand on the M62/M6 corridors, but it is operational space for Peel's own use, not lettable investment stock.

label: NORTH WEST INDUSTRIAL
headline: Aviva tables revised plans for 400,000 sq ft Manchester industrial
summary: Aviva has submitted revised plans for 400,000 sq ft of industrial space in five units on the former Ferranti factory at Styal Road and Simonsway, near Manchester Airport. A 2023 scheme was refused over Green Belt encroachment and airport safety concerns; the new design has been changed following consultation earlier this year. (Earlier coverage, included in this first news edition.)
key_figures: 400,000 sq ft across 5 units; site near Manchester Airport; 2023 application refused
relevance: Potential large-scale institutional-backed supply in the South Manchester / M56 market.
why_matters: If approved, this would be one of the largest institutional industrial schemes in Greater Manchester, adding supply to the tight M56 airport sub-market. Its progress will test planning risk for industrial schemes near Green Belt and airport safeguarding zones.

label: FINANCE / CAPITAL MARKETS
headline: SevenCitiesLdn wins £163m loan against Victoria Street office
summary: SevenCitiesLdn has secured a £163m senior whole loan from Patron Capital to support its £211m acquisition and repositioning of 123 Victoria Street, a fully let 244,000 sq ft office bought from Landsec. The facility comprises a £148m acquisition tranche and £15m for refurbishment, at 70% loan-to-cost and 59% loan-to-projected value.
key_figures: £163m loan; £211m purchase; 244,000 sq ft; 70% LTC; 59% LTV (projected)
relevance: Evidence that large-ticket office debt is available, from private credit at relatively high leverage.

label: NORTH WEST INDUSTRIAL
headline: Langtree hands over final £25m phase at Hollinwood Junction
summary: Russell WBHO has completed 192,000 sq ft of industrial space at Hollinwood Junction, Oldham (M60), forward-funded by Indurent and delivered by Langtree with Oldham Council. The £25m final phase comprises 13 units from about 5,000 sq ft to 42,000 sq ft. (Earlier coverage, included in this first news edition.)
key_figures: 192,000 sq ft; 13 units, 5,000–42,000 sq ft; £25m phase; forward-funded by Indurent
relevance: New multi-let supply in Greater Manchester; forward funding shows institutional appetite for small/mid-box.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: L&G and Verdion get green light for £30m Greenwich logistics hub
summary: Legal & General's Industrial Property Investment Fund and Verdion have won consent for LiteHub Greenwich, a £30m multi-let scheme of 78,986 sq ft in six units of 5,555–16,000 sq ft on a 2.6-acre brownfield site in West Thamesmead. Completion is targeted for Q4 2027, aiming for BREEAM Excellent and EPC A+.
key_figures: 78,986 sq ft; 6 units 5,555–16,000 sq ft; £30m; 2.6 acres; ready Q4 2027
relevance: Institutional capital continuing to back speculative urban multi-let development.

label: UK INDUSTRIAL
headline: Padrock secures 71,530 sq ft letting of south-east London warehouse
summary: Padrock has let Erith Logistics Hub, a 71,530 sq ft single-unit development in south-east London, to tabletop manufacturer Nevilles on a 15-year lease. Nevilles will move from its existing Erith premises in April and use the unit as its headquarters and global distribution centre. Padrock described the market as challenging.
key_figures: 71,530 sq ft; 15-year lease; occupation April 2027; rent not disclosed
relevance: Long-lease letting of speculative London mid-box space; occupier relocating locally.

label: PROPERTY INVESTMENT
headline: London leads European investment despite slow recovery, PwC and ULI find
summary: PwC and ULI's Emerging Trends in Real Estate Europe survey of 1,498 professionals keeps London top of the city rankings, but expects recovery to be slower and uneven. Only 45% expect higher profitability in 2027 (50% last year). Construction costs (58%) and interest rates (55%) are the leading concerns for 2027.
key_figures: 1,498 respondents; 45% expect profit growth in 2027 (50% prior); construction costs cited by 58%; interest rates by 55%
relevance: Sentiment indicator: investor confidence softening as rates and build costs bite.

label: PROPERTY INVESTMENT
headline: Seneca acquires Lawnswood Business Park in Leeds
summary: Seneca Property has bought the 150,000 sq ft Lawnswood Business Park, north Leeds, for an undisclosed sum; it was marketed at a £20m guide. The vendor, Hillview Real Estate, paid £26.5m in 2018. The park is 81% let to 17 tenants and will be refurbished into smaller fitted suites.
key_figures: 150,000 sq ft; guide £20m vs £26.5m paid in 2018; 81% occupied; 17 tenants
relevance: Regional out-of-town office pricing evidence: c.25% below 2018 price on guide basis.

label: OFFICES
headline: Office owner-occupancy reaches decade high, says Carter Jonas
summary: Carter Jonas research shows owner-occupiers took 13.4% of UK office sales by transaction count in 2025, a decade high. Outside London the share rose to 17.8% (2024 to September 2026) from 13.4% (2018–23); in London from 8.5% to 10.6%. It attributes the shift to lower capital values alongside rising rents.
relevance: Repriced regional offices are attracting owner-occupier buyers, adding liquidity below institutional lot sizes.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Birmingham's £2.2bn Ladywood regeneration plans axed over viability pressures
summary: Berkeley Group and Birmingham City Council have terminated the development agreement for the £2.2bn Ladywood Estate regeneration, a 148-acre, 20-year scheme for more than 10,000 homes. They cite increased construction and regulatory costs and a more challenged housing market and economy as putting significant pressure on viability.
key_figures: £2.2bn; 148 acres; 10,000+ homes; c.20% affordable; 20-year programme
relevance: Viability failure on a flagship scheme; cost inflation is breaking development appraisals.
why_matters: When a developer of Berkeley's scale walks away on viability, it shows that build costs and rates are breaking long-dated appraisals. The same pressures apply to speculative industrial schemes: exit yields are drifting out while costs stay high, so more projects will need pre-lets or forward funding to proceed.

label: UK INDUSTRIAL
headline: Richborough Commercial secures major appeal win on M42 corridor scheme
summary: Richborough Commercial has won outline consent at appeal for up to 700,000 sq ft of B2/B8 floorspace near M42 Junction 9 in North Warwickshire, after appealing against non-determination of a June 2024 application. Richborough says it is the first appeal allowing a major industrial and logistics scheme on grey-belt land since the revised NPPF in August. (Published before the last briefing but not previously reported.)
key_figures: Up to 700,000 sq ft B2/B8; M42 J9; outline consent on appeal; grey-belt land
relevance: Planning precedent for logistics on grey-belt land.
why_matters: A first grey-belt appeal win for logistics could unlock land supply around constrained cores, including Green Belt-heavy Greater Manchester and Cheshire. That raises land-value expectations for promoters but should, over time, ease the supply shortage that has supported North West rents.

label: UK INDUSTRIAL
headline: BARJANE submits plans for 420,000 sq ft DHL warehouse
summary: BARJANE has applied for a 420,000 sq ft logistics scheme at Ansty, Coventry, next to Frasers Group's approved 3.3m sq ft headquarters. DHL Supply Chain has agreed to occupy the BREEAM Outstanding, EPC A warehouse if planning permission is granted, giving the scheme a conditional pre-let at the M6/M69 junction. (Published before the last briefing but not previously reported.)
key_figures: 420,000 sq ft; conditional pre-let to DHL Supply Chain; Ansty, Coventry; BREEAM Outstanding target
relevance: Large-format 3PL demand being met by pre-let development rather than existing stock.
why_matters: Big-box demand is turning into pre-let development rather than speculative space. This is the route North West schemes above 300,000 sq ft are likely to need while exit yields sit at 5.50%+.

label: PROPERTY INVESTMENT
headline: Custodian REIT acquires £11m portfolio from syndicated investment vehicles
summary: Custodian Property Income REIT has bought eight fully let retail and industrial properties, mainly in the East Midlands, for £11m from syndicates managed by Lincoln Property Syndicates. The £800,000 rent reflects a 6.7% net initial yield and 7.2% reversionary yield, funded largely by issuing 10.6m new shares plus £400,000 cash. (Published before the last briefing but not previously reported.)
key_figures: £11m; 8 assets; NIY 6.7%; reversionary yield 7.2%; WAULT 6 yrs; avg lot £1.4m
relevance: Pricing evidence for small-lot regional industrial/retail: c.6.7% NIY.

label: OFFICES
headline: Criterion snaps up New London House for 500-room hotel conversion
summary: Criterion Capital's Zedwell Hotels has bought New London House, an 89,722 sq ft office on Fenchurch Street in the City, from Whitbread for an undisclosed sum, and plans to convert it into a 509-room hotel. Zedwell says it targets structurally sound, well-located buildings where conversion unlocks value. (Published before the last briefing but not previously reported.)
key_figures: 89,722 sq ft office; 509-room hotel conversion; price undisclosed
relevance: Continued removal of secondary City office stock via change of use.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Bolton pursues legal challenge into national planning changes
summary: Bolton Council has complied 'under protest' with the National Scheme of Delegation, which makes planning officers the default decision-makers for most applications. It voted to cost a judicial review and to write to all English planning authorities seeking a coordinated legal challenge against the government.
key_figures: Applies to most planning applications; judicial review being costed
relevance: Planning-process uncertainty in Greater Manchester; delegation should speed routine industrial consents if upheld.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: £2bn Manchester-Sheffield tunnel gets funding boost
summary: Future Works Infrastructure's Trans-Pennine Connect, a proposed 14-mile tolled dual carriageway with a tunnel between Manchester and Sheffield, has received £500,000 from the UK Dynamism Fund for feasibility work. The scheme, estimated at £2bn, would be funded by tolls and private or local-authority investors rather than central government.
key_figures: £500,000 feasibility funding; 14-mile route; c.£2bn estimated cost
relevance: Long-term trans-Pennine connectivity for logistics east of Greater Manchester; early-stage only.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: B&Q to cut 63,000 sq ft in Bolton as it looks to right-size
summary: BNP Paribas has applied to subdivide B&Q's 137,000 sq ft Kay Street store in Bolton into three units, cutting B&Q's space by 63,000 sq ft. Aldi would take a new 20,000 sq ft store, relocating from Higher Bridge Street, using space currently occupied by B&Q's Trade Point facility.
key_figures: 137,000 sq ft store; B&Q to give up 63,000 sq ft; 20,000 sq ft Aldi
relevance: Retail-warehouse right-sizing in Greater Manchester; large-box space being recycled to discount food.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Mansell collapsed with debts of £4.2m
summary: An administrator's report from RSM shows Oldham-based off-site construction specialist Mansell Building Solutions collapsed with debts of £4.2m, including £1.3m owed to NatWest. It entered administration in August after 36 years, citing the cost of relocating its headquarters to Oldham, Covid's impact on revenues and planning delays. Creditors include steel-framing supplier Voestalpine Metsec (£550,000).
key_figures: Debts £4.2m; £1.3m owed to NatWest; Voestalpine Metsec £550,000; CCF £220,000
relevance: Supply-chain fragility in North West construction; contractor insolvency risk for developers.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Meanwhile use put forward ahead of £250m Crompton Place regen
summary: Bolton Council plans street-food markets, a big screen and an urban garden on the Victoria Square frontage of the former Crompton Place shopping centre once it is demolished, as MEPC (part of Federated Hermes) leads a £250m regeneration. CBRE and Chapman Taylor designed the meanwhile-use strategy to keep the area active during redevelopment.
key_figures: £250m regeneration; MEPC/Federated Hermes; meanwhile use by CBRE and Chapman Taylor
relevance: Institutional-backed town-centre regeneration in Greater Manchester; retail space being repurposed.

label: PROPERTY INVESTMENT
headline: Regional cities on course for highest investment volumes in four years
summary: Avison Young's Big Nine report shows £344m of office deals in Q3 across nine regional cities including Manchester and Liverpool, taking 2026 volumes to £1.1bn, 25% ahead of the same period in 2025. Volumes are on track for the highest year since 2022, though further Bank of England rate rises could limit the final total.
key_figures: Q3 £344m; YTD £1.1bn (+25% y/y); 2022 total over £2bn; two Birmingham deals totalled £148m
relevance: Regional office investment recovery, including Manchester and Liverpool; rate rises the main risk.
why_matters: It is the clearest sign yet that investors are returning to regional offices, including Manchester, after repricing. With Knight Frank's regional prime yield at 7.00%+, buyers see income value, though another BoE hike could stall the recovery.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Wrenman wins Grey Belt appeal against Lancaster
summary: The Planning Inspectorate has overturned Lancaster City Council's refusal of Wrenman Strategic Land's outline plans for up to 200 homes on 28 acres of Green Belt at Bolton-le-Sands. The key question was whether the site counted as Grey Belt, land that does not strongly check sprawl or stop towns merging; the inspector sided with the developer against councillors.
key_figures: Up to 200 homes; 28 acres; council refusal (Feb 2026) overturned on appeal
relevance: Second grey-belt appeal win this month after the M42 logistics case; tests Green Belt release in Lancashire.
why_matters: Two grey-belt appeal wins in a fortnight, one for logistics on the M42 and now this one in Lancashire, suggest inspectors are applying the new test in developers' favour. That improves prospects for Green Belt-edge industrial land on the M6 and M61 corridors and should be priced into land-promotion and option deals.

label: UK INDUSTRIAL
headline: Rankeilour secures over £20m for UK warehouse fund
summary: Rankeilour has raised more than £20m, giving its fund about £40m to buy single and multi-let industrial and retail warehouse assets across Scotland and the North of England. It bought a Cumbernauld asset for about £5.5m off-market, with two more deals close, and targets value-add lots of £1m–6m over the next year.
key_figures: £20m+ raised; c.£40m spending power; target lots £1m–6m; Cumbernauld purchase c.£5.5m
relevance: Private-investor demand for higher-yielding Northern warehouse stock in small lots.
why_matters: It adds a new buyer for the £1–6m multi-let and secondary warehouse lots that dominate North West agency stock. That supports liquidity and pricing below institutional lot sizes while bank debt remains expensive.

label: FINANCE / CAPITAL MARKETS
headline: Regional REIT cuts debt following £32m of disposals
summary: Regional REIT has cut gross borrowings by £33.1m to £233.1m after £32.2m of disposals in the first nine months of 2026, with £8.9m sold at an average 8.3% net initial yield. Sale prices averaged 11% below pre-sale book value. Net LTV fell to 38.5% from 40.4% at end-2025, and gross asset value slipped to £516.6m.
key_figures: Disposals £32.2m YTD; sales at 8.3% NIY; 11% below book; LTV 38.5%; GAV £516.6m
relevance: Regional secondary office pricing evidence: sales clearing well below book at c.8%+ yields.

label: OFFICES
headline: MSB Solicitors makes 9,500 sq ft Liverpool switch
summary: MSB Solicitors has moved its Liverpool head office from 6,100 sq ft at No.4 St Paul's to 9,500 sq ft on the seventh floor of Forma Real Estate's No.5 St Paul's, on a 10-year lease at £26.50 per sq ft. It was Liverpool's largest office deal in Q3. Worthington Owen advised both parties.
key_figures: 9,500 sq ft; 10-year lease; £26.50/sq ft; largest Liverpool office letting in Q3
relevance: Liverpool office rental evidence; occupier upsizing within the core.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Update on £81m Central Docks in Liverpool
summary: GRAHAM is on track to finish the infrastructure for Peel Waters' 2,350-home Central Docks neighbourhood in 2028, a year after starting on site. Peel is investing £25.9m and Homes England £55.2m. Central Docks is part of the £5bn Liverpool Waters scheme, planned to include 1.2m sq ft of offices and 6.6m sq ft of residential space.
key_figures: £81m infrastructure (Peel £25.9m, Homes England £55.2m); 2,350 homes; Liverpool Waters 1.2m sq ft offices
relevance: Long-term Liverpool waterfront supply pipeline, publicly part-funded.

label: NORTH WEST INDUSTRIAL
headline: Indurent tables proposals for 840,000 sq ft Heywood shed
summary: Blackstone-backed Indurent has applied to Rochdale Council for up to 838,000 sq ft of industrial space on a 40-acre plot at Heywood Distribution Park (M62 J19). Three existing units, including the 108,000 sq ft Great Bear shed, would be demolished. One option shows three units of 418,000, 286,000 and 106,000 sq ft, alongside separate plans for 500,000 sq ft to the east.
key_figures: Up to 838,000 sq ft; 40 acres; option of 418k/286k/106k sq ft units; adjacent 500,000 sq ft plans; Heywood Distribution Park 200 acres
relevance: Major big-box supply pipeline on the M62 corridor; redevelopment of obsolete stock.
why_matters: It is the largest North West industrial proposal for some time, and together with the 500,000 sq ft to the east it could add over 1.3m sq ft of modern space on the M62. It eases the region's Grade A shortage over time, but delivery will depend on pre-lets while exit yields sit at 5.50%+ and gilts above 5.3%.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Landsec 'optimistic' about Mayfield in face of development challenges
summary: Reporting stable half-year profits of £192m, Landsec said the second office at its Mayfield scheme in Manchester could start next year, but its 900 homes will not begin before 2028. Citing high interest rates, the Building Safety Act and construction cost inflation, it has cut development to under 2% of its portfolio. Retail rents rose 6.3%.
key_figures: Half-year earnings £192m; EPRA NTA 893p (882p); development <2% of portfolio; Mayfield homes not before 2028; retail rents +6.3%
relevance: Manchester office pipeline timing; major REIT retreating from development on cost and rates.
why_matters: A FTSE 100 developer is cutting development to under 2% of its book on rates and costs while still advancing a Manchester office. That shows where conviction remains: prime city-centre offices with pre-let prospects. It is the same logic that will govern speculative North West industrial starts.

label: UK INDUSTRIAL
headline: Plans for jumbo tissue manufacturing plant in Yorkshire binned
summary: Finnish manufacturer Metsä Tissue has abandoned plans for the UK's largest tissue paper mill, a 3m sq ft facility on a 211-acre site in Goole, East Yorkshire, only two months after planning approval in September. First announced in 2023, the project had been described as an investment of several hundred million pounds.
key_figures: 3m sq ft; 211 acres; consented September 2026; investment 'several hundred million pounds'
relevance: Large manufacturing investment withdrawn; signals cost and demand caution among industrial occupiers.

label: NORTH WEST INDUSTRIAL
headline: First phase of delayed £40m Leyland industrial completes
summary: About 23,000 sq ft across 19 units has been handed over at the 190,000 sq ft Titan Business Park, Leyland, which was originally due in 2022. Funder Pitalia has taken control from developer Providence Gate. Six units of about 2,300 sq ft are to let and 13 of 750 sq ft are for sale; the remaining 167,000 sq ft is due to start next year.
key_figures: Phase 1 c.23,000 sq ft / 19 units; scheme 190,000 sq ft; £40m; 167,000 sq ft to start 2027; agents Turner Westwell, Robert Pinkus & Co
relevance: Small-unit supply in Lancashire; delivery delays and funder step-in show development risk.

label: OFFICES
headline: London's office market take-up hits two year high of 3m sq ft, C&W finds
summary: Cushman & Wakefield's Central London Offices Marketbeat shows Q3 take-up above 3m sq ft, up 25% on Q2 and 24% ahead of the five-year average. The City took 1.9m sq ft and the West End 1.1m sq ft. Year-to-date take-up of nearly 7.5m sq ft is 11% higher than a year earlier.
key_figures: Q3 3m+ sq ft (+25% q/q; +24% vs 5-yr avg); City 1.9m; West End 1.1m; YTD 7.5m sq ft (+11%)
relevance: Strong occupier demand for London offices despite higher rates.

label: PROPERTY INVESTMENT
headline: GPE sells Clifford Chance's London headquarters to Rothesay for £422.3m
source: Great Portland Estates RNS via Investegate
summary: GPE has sold 2 Aldermanbury Square, a 324,700 sq ft City headquarters office let to Clifford Chance until 2046, to annuity insurer Rothesay for a headline £422.3m. That reflects a 5.25% net initial yield, or £368.7m net of outstanding rent-frees, around 3% ahead of March 2026 book value. The building is on a 180-year geared ground lease.
key_figures: £422.3m headline (£368.7m net); NIY 5.25%; 324,700 sq ft; let to 2046; c.3% above March book value
relevance: Prime long-let City office pricing at 5.25% NIY, achieved despite the gilt sell-off; matched-income buyer.
why_matters: A 5.25% yield on a 20-year City letting, struck as gilts hit 5.3%+, shows long-dated matching capital (insurers and annuity funds) will still pay near-gilt yields for secure income. It is the strongest evidence this month that the best long-income assets are not repricing as fast as bonds.

label: NORTH WEST INDUSTRIAL
headline: HMG seeks £12.6m for GM industrial trio
summary: Hollins Murray Group has appointed King Street Real Estate to sell three Greater Manchester industrial units at a £12.6m guide. They are Caxton Close, Wigan (46,300 sq ft, let to Velocity Leisure as a padel venue), Carrs House, Bredbury (35,600 sq ft, recently let to DPD for five years) and a refurbished, vacant 24,500 sq ft unit at Stakehill.
key_figures: £12.6m guide; 3 units totalling 106,400 sq ft; DPD five-year lease at Bredbury; Stakehill vacant
relevance: New North West multi-asset industrial investment on the market; a test of small-lot pricing.
why_matters: It is a live test of North West small-lot industrial pricing after the gilt sell-off. The price achieved against the £12.6m guide will show whether private and fund buyers such as Rankeilour are absorbing higher rates. Short leases and a vacant unit make it a value-add rather than core lot.

label: FINANCE / CAPITAL MARKETS
headline: Kadans and CWG secure £368m for flagship Canary Wharf life sciences scheme
summary: Canary Wharf Group and Kadans Science Partner have secured £368.5m of development debt for One North Quay, a 23-storey, c.570,000 sq ft life sciences and workspace building due for completion in early 2028. The government's National Wealth Fund provided £147m alongside Barclays and Emirates NBD.
key_figures: £368.5m debt; National Wealth Fund £147m; Barclays, Emirates NBD; 570,000 sq ft; completion early 2028
relevance: State-backed capital filling gaps in development finance for strategic schemes.
why_matters: It shows large development finance now depends on public co-lenders as bank appetite narrows. North West schemes with growth or innovation credentials, such as GMCA growth locations, may need similar blended funding to proceed.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: GMCA seeks consultant to kick off spatial development strategy
summary: Greater Manchester Combined Authority is seeking a consultant (£150,000 commission) for an integrated impact assessment to underpin its statutory spatial development strategy. Required under the Planning and Infrastructure Act, the SDS will identify strategic growth locations for the next 25 years and support the six growth locations in GM's £10bn pipeline, going beyond Places for Everyone.
key_figures: £150,000 commission; 25-year horizon; six growth locations; £10bn pipeline
relevance: Long-term framework for Greater Manchester employment-land allocations.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Bury submits local plan to govt
summary: Bury Council has voted to submit its local plan, covering the period to 2043, to the Planning Inspectorate, putting it on course for adoption in November 2027. That would be Bury's first adopted local plan since 1997. The plan sets policies on affordable housing, transport, biodiversity net gain and flood risk.
key_figures: Plan period to 2043; adoption targeted Nov 2027; first local plan since 1997
relevance: Planning certainty improving in Greater Manchester boroughs.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Rochdale's Seven Sisters to be knocked down as refurb estimates hit £269m
summary: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing will demolish the seven 1960s College Bank tower blocks (766 bedsits) after estimating retrofit costs of at least £269m, around £388,000 a flat. Around 600 new homes will replace them once residents are rehoused by next summer.
key_figures: Retrofit cost £269m+ (c.£388k per flat); 766 bedsits; c.600 replacement homes
relevance: Retrofit economics favouring demolition; cost inflation theme.

label: PROPERTY INVESTMENT
headline: Allsop raises £35.6m at penultimate commercial auction of the year
summary: Allsop sold 41 lots for more than £35.6m at its penultimate commercial auction of 2026, an 84% success rate, with regional assets almost two-thirds of lots. The largest deal was a Southampton town-centre parade (tenants include Tesco Express, HMV and The Gym Group), sold before auction for £4.1m at a 10.7% NIY.
key_figures: £35.6m; 41 lots; 84% success rate; largest £4.1m at 10.7% NIY
relevance: Private-investor liquidity for high-yield secondary stock remains good.

label: UK INDUSTRIAL
headline: Sirius reports 17.9% revenue rise as it eyes future UK acquisitions
summary: Sirius Real Estate, which owns business and industrial parks in Germany and the UK, reported a 17.9% rise in half-year revenue to €191.4m. Pre-tax profit before revaluations rose 39.3% to €60m, but a €24m valuation deficit cut reported pre-tax profit to €36m. The group is targeting further UK acquisitions.
key_figures: Revenue €191.4m (+17.9%); underlying PBT €60m (+39.3%); valuation deficit €24m; reported PBT €36m
relevance: Listed multi-let industrial owner: income growing while values ease.

label: NORTH WEST INDUSTRIAL
headline: New home for saved gas meter outfit
summary: Utility Meters Warehouse, bought out of administration by Energy Assets, has signed a five-year lease on 17,000 sq ft (15,600 sq ft warehouse, 1,000 sq ft office) at Unit 6 Kiwi Court, Trafford Park, at £13 per sq ft. It relocates from Leo Industrial Estate nearby and roughly doubles its space. Davies Harrison advised the private landlord.
key_figures: 17,000 sq ft; £13.00/sq ft; 5-year lease; Kiwi Court, Trafford Park; landlord agent Davies Harrison
relevance: Trafford Park mid-box rental evidence at £13/sq ft on a short lease.
why_matters: It is fresh Trafford Park rental evidence: £13 per sq ft for a 17,000 sq ft second-hand unit on a five-year lease. That supports current North West mid-box ERVs despite the rates shock and is a direct comparable for lettings and rent reviews in the M60 core.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Liverpool to run rule over Peel's scaled back vision for Liverpool Waters
summary: Peel Waters has cut the total development in its 150-acre Liverpool Waters masterplan, adopted 13 years ago, by about 8m sq ft. Changes include about 2m sq ft less office space and homes reduced to 7,111 from 9,000, partly because Everton's stadium occupies former residential land. Liverpool's planning committee considers the changes next week.
key_figures: c.8m sq ft reduction; offices down c.2m sq ft; homes 7,111 (from 9,000); c.1,300 homes delivered since 2013
relevance: Long-term Liverpool supply pipeline shrinking, especially offices.
why_matters: Cutting about 2m sq ft of planned offices recognises weaker long-run office demand and viability on the waterfront. Less future supply supports existing Liverpool city-centre office stock, but it also signals that big masterplans are being right-sized to today's costs and rates.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Feedback wanted on Warrington local plan
summary: Warrington has opened its second consultation, running to 11 January, on a local plan to 2039 allocating land for 13,250 homes and 586 acres of employment space. It accepts some Green Belt release is needed, and an AECOM study identified 362 areas of existing Green Belt that could qualify as Grey Belt.
key_figures: 586 acres employment land; 13,250 homes; plan to 2039; 362 potential Grey Belt areas; consultation closes 11 Jan
relevance: Major future employment-land supply on the M6/M62 hub.
why_matters: With 586 acres of employment land at the M6/M62/M56 junction, Warrington's plan will shape North West logistics supply for a decade. The Grey Belt assessment, after two appeal wins this month, gives landowners and promoters a window to put forward sites before 11 January.

label: UK INDUSTRIAL
headline: Aberdeen Investments buys £25m Arrow Point industrial asset in Crawley
summary: Aberdeen Investments has bought Arrow Point in Crawley's Manor Royal Business District for £25m for the Standard Life Pooled Pension Property Fund. The modern units, with 8–12m eaves, 30–40m yards, EPC A and BREEAM Very Good ratings, are fully let to Blueleaf and Leo Cancer Care. The yield was not disclosed.
key_figures: £25m; fully let; EPC A; BREEAM Very Good; yield undisclosed
relevance: Institutional pension capital still buying modern multi-let industrial in the South East.

label: UK INDUSTRIAL
headline: Henry Boot secures Walsall warehouse letting for Origin portfolio
summary: HBD, Henry Boot's development arm, has let a 39,000 sq ft warehouse at SPARK Walsall to wholesaler Tican, after deals with Relay Tech and E.ON UK. The scheme is part of Origin, its industrial joint venture with Feldberg Capital, which is now 67% let across its 711,000 sq ft portfolio.
key_figures: 39,000 sq ft letting; Origin portfolio 711,000 sq ft, 67% let
relevance: Speculative Midlands mid-box space letting steadily but with a third still vacant.

label: PROPERTY INVESTMENT
headline: Custodian REIT reports robust performance with steady rental growth
summary: Custodian Property Income REIT reported 0.7% like-for-like ERV growth in the quarter to September and 1.7% for the first half of its financial year. Industrial, 42% of income, led with 1.3% quarterly ERV growth, despite what the REIT called ongoing macroeconomic uncertainty.
key_figures: ERV +0.7% (quarter), +1.7% (H1); industrial ERV +1.3% (quarter); industrial 42% of income
relevance: Regional multi-sector rental growth continues, led by industrial.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Landsec puts 18-month freeze on major residential and office developments
summary: Follow-up to Landsec's results: Landsec will freeze major new residential and office development for 18 months, saying returns no longer offer sufficient upside. Its results presentation cited a 41% rise in London office construction costs over five years while prime London office values have been flat.
key_figures: 18-month freeze; London office build costs +41% in 5 years; prime values flat
relevance: Quantifies the cost-versus-value squeeze on development.

label: FINANCE / CAPITAL MARKETS
headline: GREYKITE sells minority stake in pan-European logistics platform to BSP
summary: Greykite European Real Estate Fund I has sold a minority stake in its Silverdock pan-European logistics platform to Benefit Street Partners, part of Franklin Templeton, for an undisclosed sum. Silverdock has assembled 26 assets totalling over 7.53m sq ft since late 2024, mainly in Germany, France and the UK.
key_figures: 26 assets; 7.53m sq ft; launched late 2024; price undisclosed
relevance: Private credit and equity still committing to logistics platforms.

label: PROPERTY INVESTMENT
headline: British Land confirms organisational restructure and potential job cuts as earnings rise
summary: British Land reported half-year underlying profit up 7% to £166m, with 12% like-for-like net rental growth, EPRA NTA up 2% to 599p and ERV growth of 3.0%. Its portfolio rose 1.5% to £10.5bn and the net equivalent yield moved out 3bp to 6.1%. It is restructuring to save £5–7m a year, with up to 50 job cuts reported.
key_figures: Underlying profit £166m (+7%); NTA 599p (+2%); LTV 39.6%; ERV +3.0%; NEY 6.1% (+3bp); like-for-like net rents +12%
relevance: Listed evidence that rental growth is offsetting yield pressure in campuses, retail parks and London urban logistics.
why_matters: British Land's valuations rose despite gilts above 5%, because 3% ERV growth outweighed a 3bp outward yield shift. That is the mechanism North West industrial owners need: rental growth carrying values while yields drift. It supports income-led valuations at the December quarter-end.

label: PROPERTY INVESTMENT
headline: Penrith M&S on sale for £5m
summary: Carrick Real Estate is seeking offers above £5m for the M&S store in Penrith, let on a 20-year lease from 2015 at about £400,000 a year, reflecting a 7.5% net initial yield at the asking price. The BAE Systems Pension Scheme bought it from LondonMetric for £6.7m in 2018.
key_figures: £5m+ asking; c.£400,000 rent; NIY 7.5%; bought for £6.7m in 2018
relevance: North West regional retail pricing evidence: about 25% below 2018 value.
why_matters: A 7.5% yield for a long M&S lease in Cumbria, about 25% below its 2018 price, shows how far regional long-income pricing has adjusted. It is a useful benchmark for North West investors comparing retail warehouse and industrial yields.

label: OFFICES
headline: Domis tops out 43-storey No2 St Michael's
summary: Domis Construction has topped out the 43-storey No2 St Michael's in central Manchester, the tower element of the £400m Salboy and Relentless Developments scheme, due to complete next year. It includes 75,000 sq ft of offices, building on the fully let 185,000 sq ft No1 St Michael's, plus a 162-room W Hotel and 217 W-branded residences.
key_figures: 43 storeys; £400m scheme; 75,000 sq ft workspace; No1 St Michael's 185,000 sq ft fully let; completion 2027
relevance: New Grade A office supply in Manchester city centre in 2027.
why_matters: It adds 75,000 sq ft of Grade A Manchester office space next year, alongside a fully let first phase. That points to continued occupier demand for the best city-centre space even as Landsec and others freeze speculative development.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Lancashire signs off £643m transport proposals
summary: Lancashire Combined County Authority has unanimously approved its Local Transport Plan implementation plan for 2026–2030, worth £643m, with rail station improvements and rural connectivity prominent. Officers will now deliver the four-year programme, informed by public consultation on the publication version.
key_figures: £643m programme; 2026–2030; unanimous approval
relevance: Infrastructure spend supporting Lancashire employment locations over four years.

label: OFFICES
headline: Workspace Group's losses widen to £121.2m as strategic turnaround progresses
summary: Workspace Group reported a £121.2m pre-tax loss for the half-year, 70% wider than a year earlier, driven by a 6.6% fall in portfolio value from £2.13bn to £1.96bn. It deferred its interim dividend decision but reported 'good early signs' from its turnaround strategy for its London flexible-office business.
key_figures: Loss £121.2m (+70.4%); portfolio £1.96bn (-6.6%); interim dividend deferred
relevance: London flexible/SME office values still falling.

label: PROPERTY INVESTMENT
headline: Praxis snaps up Cardiff's Morgan Quarter in £27.2m deal
summary: Praxis has bought Morgan Quarter in Cardiff, a 158,000 sq ft freehold including the grade II-listed Royal and Morgan Arcades and the Creative Quarter office hub, for £27.2m. It plans £5m of capital investment to upgrade flexible workspace for local SMEs.
key_figures: £27.2m; 158,000 sq ft; £5m capex planned
relevance: Value-add capital buying regional mixed-use stock.
